official.title: Postdoc User Acceptance of Automated Buses
official.description_text:
Study how passengers experience automated buses and help evaluate a new service connecting Delft Campus station and the TU Delft campus.
Job description
This postdoc position is part of an international project aimed at automated bus transport. Automated buses have proven they can drive safely, but most still require onboard staff because supervision, safety assurance, and regulatory requirements must be met before driverless operation is possible. The project aims to remove this barrier by combining remote supervision, passenger safety monitoring, and fleet management into a single operational framework. With demonstrations in Switzerland, the Netherlands, and the United Kingdom, the project aims to create deployment-ready solutions that can be scaled after 2030. Automated bus transport is essential to maintain and expand public transport services, enabling operators to deliver more public transport while supporting accessible and zero-emission mobility. For the demonstration in the Netherlands, the project plans to study an automated bus service connecting the train station Delft Campus to the TU Delft premises.
As postdoctoral researcher you will focus on the acceptance of automated buses. To apply vehicle automation in public transport at a larger scale, it is essential to carefully assess the acceptance by end users, understand the contribution of vehicle automation to the overall public transport system (for instance as first/last kilometer) and evaluate the lessons learned on the demonstration sites. Specific tasks are: (1) definition of the impact assessment and evaluation plan, (2) conducting research into user acceptance and positioning in the public transport system, (3) consolidate lessons learned from the demonstration sites and (4) produce a final dissemination report. Specific emphasis will be on the demonstration site in the Netherlands, working with DAM Shuttles and supported by the concession provider MRDH, the city of Delft and public transport operators RET and HTM. As postdoctoral researcher you will also write scientific papers and present results at conferences.
At TU Delft you will be part of the Sustainable Urban Multimodal mobility (SUM) Lab in the Department of Transport & Planning.
Job requirements
You have obtained your PhD degree in transport or a related field.
You have experience with user acceptance of automated transport and public transport systems.
You have the capability and experience to work independently as well as with public and private parties.
You have excellent English language and communication skills.
Preferably you possess Dutch language skills and familiarity with the Dutch transport system and context.
TU Delft (Delft University of Technology)
Working at TU Delft means contributing to solutions that really make a difference.
For over 180 years, we have been training engineers who make an impact worldwide in companies, government bodies, or as entrepreneurs. Our alumni turn knowledge into concrete solutions for the challenges of today and tomorrow. These challenges are changing rapidly. That is why we focus on themes such as energy, climate, digitalisation, artificial intelligence (AI), and smart mobility every day. Our education and research are directly aligned with what society needs now and in the future.
At TU Delft, our people make the difference. With their knowledge and curiosity, our staff provide a high-quality education and conduct pioneering research that extends beyond the campus. You will have the opportunity to take the initiative, work with others, and grow as a professional. Working at TU Delft means join an international community of professionals and students. Together, we create knowledge, innovations, and solutions that help move the world forward.
Faculty of Civil Engineering and Geosciences
The Faculty of Civil Engineering & Geosciences (CEG) is committed to outstanding international research and education in the field of civil engineering, applied earth sciences, traffic and transport, water technology, and delta technology. Our research feeds into our educational programmes and covers societal challenges such as climate change, energy transition, resource availability, urbanisation and clean water. Our research projects are conducted in close cooperation with a wide range of research institutions. CEG is convinced of the importance of open science and supports its scientists in integrating open science in their research practice. The Faculty of CEG comprises 28 research groups in the following seven departments: Materials Mechanics Management & Design, Engineering Structures, Geoscience and Engineering, Geoscience and Remote Sensing, Transport & Planning, Hydraulic Engineering and Water Management.

ai.summary: Postdoctoral position (2 years, 21–24 hrs/week) evaluating user acceptance of automated buses and their role in public transport systems. Work includes impact assessment design, user acceptance research, evaluation at three demonstration sites (Switzerland, Netherlands, UK), and dissemination; focus on Netherlands site with DAM Shuttles connecting Delft station to TU Delft campus.

thematic_fit.rationale: Modest thematic overlap. Position focuses on user acceptance and human factors in automated transport—a human-centred perspective. However, core themes diverge: researcher's target is spatial cognition, immersive learning, collaborative systems, and wayfinding; this position addresses acceptance of autonomous vehicle technology and public transport integration. Thematic connection is via user-centred research mindset, but domains (immersive learning vs. transport automation) are distinct. No XR, immersion, collaboration, or spatial-learning dimensions.

methodological_fit.rationale: Stronger methodological alignment. Position requires user acceptance research, impact assessment design, and evaluation—core strengths of researcher's Master's work (user studies, experimental design, usability and technology acceptance). Researcher has intermediate user-studies and experimental-design skills directly applicable. However, domain is transport/HCI (vehicles, services, systems) rather than immersive systems. Transport acceptance literature and stakeholder engagement (DAM Shuttles, MRDH, RET, HTM) differ from spatial-learning user research, but methodological toolkit (questionnaires, evaluation frameworks, participant studies) is transferable. Research will likely require qualitative research and mixed-methods, which researcher has not emphasized but could develop.

growth_value.rationale: Moderate growth value. Researcher would deepen user-acceptance research, impact assessment, and mixed-methods evaluation—directly building on Master's strengths. Work on stakeholder engagement and multi-site case study comparison (Switzerland, UK, Netherlands) would strengthen research communication and comparative evaluation skills. However, work does not advance core capability gaps in statistics (mixed-effects modelling) or spatial cognition theory. No XR, immersive design, or collaborative systems expertise gained. Postdoc research trajectory could develop into human-factors research in emerging technologies but diverges from spatial-learning and immersive-systems focus.

strategic_value.rationale: Good strategic positioning. TU Delft is priority-1 institution. SUM Lab (Sustainable Urban Multimodal mobility) is well-regarded in transport and sustainable mobility research. Supervisor (Prof. Bart van Arem) is established transport researcher. Funding appears secure (project already approved for demonstration). However, group culture and research agenda are transport/mobility-focused, not HCI or immersive systems. Postdoc work does not establish researcher as human-centred XR specialist but could position researcher as human factors specialist in autonomous systems, which is adjacent to target identity. International scope (three demo sites) and stakeholder collaboration with public/private partners adds career development value.

eligibility_flags: Requires PhD; researcher holds MSc by Research (not completed). Eligibility depends on whether MSc by Research is recognized as equivalent to PhD in Dutch system or if completion of thesis is required by start date (1 January 2027)
Preferred skills: Dutch language and familiarity with Dutch transport system; researcher has neither stated
risks: Career-stage gate: position requires PhD; researcher's MSc by Research may not qualify unless degree is awarded by 1 January 2027 start date
Language barrier: Dutch language skills preferred but not required; lack of Dutch may limit stakeholder engagement (MRDH, RET, HTM, city of Delft)
Domain drift: postdoc trajectory in transport acceptance, though methodologically aligned, does not establish researcher in immersive systems or spatial-learning research
Part-time commitment (21–24 hrs/week) may limit integration into full research group culture
Two-year postdoc delays entry into doctoral-level research in core target area
No XR, immersive design, or collaborative system expertise to be gained

eligibility_reasons: whether a completed degree is required before employment is not stated; your MSc is still in progress — verify with the source
